# 论文仓库：cuq-thesis

正文在 thesis/ 目录下，入口文件是 thesis/main.tex，用 pdflatex 编译。

根目录的 main.tex 是 2025 年会议摘要的一页旧稿，仅存档，不再维护，编译和修改都与它无关。

\section{Climatic Setting}
The upper Cuq basin drains 4{,}300 km$^2$ of monsoon-influenced
terrain between 1{,}900 and 4{,}100 m elevation. Annual precipitation
decreases from 900 mm at the basin outlet to below 500 mm at the
headwaters, and roughly seventy percent falls between June and
September. The seasonal concentration of rainfall makes the run-off
regime strongly monsoonal, with a single sustained high-flow period
rather than the double peak seen in snowmelt-dominated basins.

Streamflow has been gauged at the basin outlet since 1962. The record
shows a marked regime shift around 2000: mean annual run-off declined
by roughly twelve percent relative to the 1962--1999 average, while
the coefficient of variation of monthly flows increased. Whether the
decline reflects precipitation change, land-use intensification in the
mid-basin, or increased abstraction for the terrace schemes remains
unsettled, and the three hypotheses are revisited in the results
chapter.

Earlier work on the basin treated the monsoon onset date as the
dominant control on annual water yield. More recent analyses suggest
that run-off generation is more sensitive to the intra-seasonal
distribution of storms than to onset timing, a distinction that
matters for the interpretation of the post-2000 record.

\section{Trend Analysis}
Trends were assessed with the Mann--Kendall test applied to annual
and seasonal aggregates, with pre-whitening to limit the influence of
serial correlation. Annual discharge shows a significant negative
trend over 1962--2020 ($p < 0.05$), driven almost entirely by the
monsoon months; the dry-season flow shows no significant trend in
either direction.

Decomposition into run-off per unit precipitation sharpens the
picture. The ratio declines steeply after 2000, indicating that the
flow reduction exceeds what the precipitation decline alone would
predict. This non-proportional response is consistent with a growing
abstraction signal, although the abstraction records needed to confirm
this directly are fragmentary before 2010.

A change-point analysis on the run-off ratio series places the most
probable break in 2001, in agreement with the expansion dates of the
two largest terrace schemes. The coincidence is suggestive rather than
conclusive, and the limitations of the abstraction record are
discussed in the following chapter.
